messages:
olivia_sales: ACME POC reporting no W3C trace ids in their exported logs from Azure Monitor — they only see our x-request-id. SRE says it's blocking POC signoff.

kevin_eng: Are they talking to hosted API or a Dedicated endpoint?

olivia_sales: Hosted (api.redwood.ai). They claim they send traceparent header but it doesn’t land.

tara_reliability: Quick checklist: 1) verify client sends `traceparent` to our ingress; 2) ensure any proxy or gateway preserves headers; 3) older SDKs may not forward out. What SDK/version?

olivia_sales: They pasted package.json: `redwood-js-sdk@1.1.3`.

kevin_eng: That SDK had a bug where the SDK rebuilds headers and can drop unknown headers. Recommend upgrade to >=1.2.1. If they can’t upgrade quickly, they can set the header on the app request before SDK call.

lee_oncall: From runtime logs they sent: `2026-02-22T15:04:12.831Z WARN incoming-request missing traceparent header request_id=p-789 origin=acme`. Points at header not reaching our front door.

tara_reliability: Also check Azure App Gateway / Application Gateway settings — some normalize or drop `traceparent` unless you allow forwarded headers. If they’re behind nginx, here’s a minimal snippet to passthrough: 
```
proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;
proxy_set_header Tracestate $http_tracestate;
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;
proxy_pass_request_headers on;
```

olivia_sales: I’ll send that plus a short KQL to correlate request ids and traces.

kevin_eng: KQL example (one-liner to join traces and requests by parsed trace): `requests | extend tp=extract("([0-9a-f]{32}-[0-9a-f]{16})",1,tostring(customDimensions.traceparent)) | join (traces | project traceId) on $left.tp == $right.traceId` — adapt table names.

support_bot: Created ticket POC-4829 and assigned to eng-trace.

lee_oncall: I’ll reproduce with SDK v1.1.3 + nginx locally and confirm; if reproducible I’ll capture a tiny hotfix curl wrapper they can use until upgrade. ETA 3h.

olivia_sales: Thanks team. I told ACME we prefer upgrade but gave nginx snippet and temp header-setting workaround. Will update once they test. :thumbsup:
